items.text: Use a right-click menu to open speaker characterization windows instead of a button, as it is more intuitive and user-friendly.
Implement a right-click menu that includes options to view all meetings a user has been in or to characterize a speaker.
Allow double-clicking on topics to automatically show all meetings containing that topic, as a default action to improve usability.
Integrate speaker characterization into the browsing experience by linking speaker traits to topics or meetings.
Evaluate and test the behavior of double-click actions on topics and speakers to determine if they should be implemented as a default action.
Investigate whether single-channel audio files should be included in the system, with a recommendation to defer integration due to increased data footprint.
Design a unified interface where transcription and summary are displayed in the same window using tabs or toggle buttons to reduce window clutter.
Explore the feasibility of implementing multiple transcript views (full meeting, meeting without disfluencies, summary) within a single window using toggle buttons.
Develop a prototype that demonstrates integration between GUI components, such as speaker characterization, topic browsing, and transcription views.
Assess the accessibility of existing GUI code to allow team members to review and build upon the latest implementation.
What is the most common use case for double-clicking on a topic or speaker in the interface?
How should speaker characterization be leveraged to improve meeting browsing and user navigation?
The team will meet next week in the morning to review progress and discuss the search interface design.
Speaker S1 will build a search interface with tick boxes and drop-down menus for search options based on agreed criteria.
The team will decide on specific search types (e.g., dialogue acts) over the weekend to define the scope of the search interface.
Speaker S1 will make the NLSSD/M browser directory readable and share it with the team.
Speaker S1 will share code and explain how the NXT search works to help others understand the transcript and summary extraction process.
Speaker S7 will share their work on reading XML files and extracting data, including challenges with file output.
Speaker S8 will explore existing code and tutorials for indexing and reusing code from tutorials.
The team will set a milestone to complete an interim prototype by June 23 (two weeks from now).
The team will research the query language to understand what search capabilities are available.
The team will meet to review the current code and basics of the project (e.g., class paths, access to corpus) as a tutorial.
The meeting will be scheduled for Monday afternoon, between 1 and 3 PM, with 3 PM being a preferred time.
The team will define a clear set of search capabilities (e.g., dialogue acts) before finalizing the interface design.
The team agrees to use a menu-based design with an LCD display, inspired by mobile phones, to simplify navigation and improve usability for all age groups.
The team decides to include a large print mode or an extra button for older users to enhance readability on the LCD screen.
The team agrees to consider a flip-top remote control design to provide a larger screen when flipped open, drawing from mobile phone design features.
S5 will document the meeting notes and store them in the shared folder for future reference.
The team will evaluate whether to undercut the price of the remote control in future iterations based on market feedback and production costs.
The team will discuss and refine the product's target market, confirming it is accessible and user-friendly for all age groups, including older adults.
The team will explore the feasibility of using a black-and-white LCD screen within the budget of €25 selling price and €12.50 production cost.
The team will assess whether the current universal remote control design, with its signal loss and complexity, presents a key design challenge to be addressed.
The team will consider whether to include both speaker characterization and topic segmentation features in the remote control software, based on user feedback.
The team will confirm the target launch timeline for the remote control, with a focus on the first year of operations and a profit aim of €15 million.
The team will evaluate the feasibility of international market expansion, including regions such as Australia and the United States, without requiring language-specific adaptations.
Can the remote control be designed to be intuitive enough for older users who are not familiar with digital interfaces or programming?
The new remote control should be original, trendy, and user-friendly.
Each team member will complete individual work on functional, conceptual, and detailed design phases before discussing them in the meeting.
Eileen and Speaker S2 will try out the whiteboard to learn how to present on it during the next meeting.
Speaker S2 will draw a cat (specifically a 'sneak' cat) as a test of the whiteboard functionality.
The selling price of the remote control will be 25 euros.
The company's profit aim is 50 million euros.
The market range is unlimited (international).
The production cost should not exceed 12.50 euros.
Speaker S2 will consider redesigning the remote control after completion of the design phase.
The remote control does not need to be fashionable or made of metal; plastic is acceptable and potentially cheaper.
Team members will introduce themselves with their name and role during the meeting.
Can the remote control be made with plastic and still look good?
